name: 05-the-rival-battle
objective: Your rival challenges you the moment you have a starter, and only when you are standing on row 6 of the laboratory. Walk down to (4,6) or (5,6) and fight him. The cartridge sets EVENT_BATTLED_RIVAL_IN_OAKS_LAB after the battle either way and heals your party, so the goal is that the battle happened, not that it was won: losing this one battle does NOT black you out, and the game says so in its own source.
evidence: watch:battled_rival_in_lab!=0 — EVENT_BATTLED_RIVAL_IN_OAKS_LAB, event index 35, so wEventFlags $D74B bit 3, mask $08. The index was walked out of pokered's constants/event_constants.asm const list, the same walk that puts EVENT_FOLLOWED_OAK_INTO_LAB at index 0 byte 0 bit 0. SetEvent EVENT_BATTLED_RIVAL_IN_OAKS_LAB is in OaksLabRivalEndBattleScript (pokered scripts/OaksLab.asm), immediately after `predef HealParty`, and that map script runs when the battle returns to the overworld whoever won.

no failure condition, and that is a correction rather than an omission. This scenario used to declare `party_hp=0` a failure, which contradicted its own objective and the cartridge: HandlePlayerBlackOut (pokered engine/battle/core.asm) special-cases this battle — `ld a,[wCurOpponent] / cp OPP_RIVAL1` then, after printing Rival1WinText, `ld a,[wCurMap] / cp OAKS_LAB / ret z`, whose own comment reads 'starter battle in oak's lab: don't black out'. The player stays in the laboratory, OaksLabRivalEndBattleScript heals the party on the next map-script tick and sets the flag, and the run continues. Failing the episode on a party at 0 HP therefore judged a state the game explicitly refuses to treat as a loss, and it was ending 166 of 600 attempts about two seconds before the goal fired.
